exercises.title: Welcome: learn the workflow
exercises.hint: This introduction is already complete. In watch mode, open the displayed file, then press `n` to continue to the first coding exercise.

exercises.title: Hello: fix the type error
exercises.hint: The function is declared to return Int, but the body returns a String. Replace the string with an integer literal.

exercises.title: Sum to n: a loop
exercises.hint: Use a `for i = 1; i <= n; i = i + 1` loop and a mutable `total` that accumulates each `i`.

exercises.title: Shape area: enums and match
exercises.hint: Match on `Circle(r)` and `Square(s)`. Use `3 * r * r` for the circle (a stand-in for pi) and `s * s` for the square.

exercises.title: Describe an option: Option and match
Safe divide: error handling
exercises.hint: Return `Err("division by zero")` when `b == 0`, otherwise `Ok(a / b)`.

exercises.title: Maximum: generics
exercises.hint: Return `a` when `a > b`, otherwise `b`. The `Compare` bound already lets you use `>`.

exercises.title: Map: higher-order functions
exercises.hint: Build a fresh array, iterate over `arr`, and push `f(x)` for each element.

exercises.title: Count evens: an array loop
exercises.hint: Iterate over `arr` and count elements where `x % 2 == 0`.

exercises.title: Greeting: string interpolation
exercises.hint: Return `"Hello, \{name}!"` so the supplied name appears in the greeting.

exercises.title: Code point count: Unicode iteration
exercises.hint: `text.length()` counts UTF-16 code units, so an emoji counts as two. Iterate over `text.iter()` and count each Unicode code point (`Char`) instead.

exercises.title: Redact digits: text processing
exercises.hint: Create a `StringBuilder`, iterate over `text.iter()`, write `'*'` for each `char.is_ascii_digit()` and otherwise write the original char, then call `to_string()`.
